english: to the problem of proving that every function which maps the interior of an oval of an algebraic curve onto a half-plane satisfies an ordinary algebraic differential equation.
topic: Prompted by a lecture of Lindemann, Hilbert considers whether every function mapping the interior of an oval of an algebraic curve onto a half-plane satisfies an ordinary algebraic differential equation, and describes Lindemann's approach and its limitation.

triage.modern_statement: Let C be a real algebraic plane curve, and let Ω be the bounded, simply connected Jordan domain enclosed by one of its ovals. Let f: Ω → H be a Riemann map onto the upper half-plane. Is f (or its inverse) always differentially algebraic? That is, is there a nonzero polynomial P with P(z, f, f', ..., f^(n)) ≡ 0? Put another way: can a Riemann map of an algebraically bounded domain ever be hypertranscendental?
triage.answered_by: No resolution identified. My searches did not find any source that proves or disproves the statement in general, and I hit the search-tool limit before I could run the most targeted searches.

evidence.claim: Related but not the same question: T. Kaiser studies the Riemann map from the upper half-plane onto a bounded, simply connected semianalytic domain. That class includes domains bounded by ovals of algebraic curves. He looks at the map's tameness (definability in an o-minimal structure), not at whether it satisfies an algebraic ODE.

For polygons (piecewise-linear boundaries, which are not ovals of a single algebraic curve), the Schwarz–Christoffel formula gives the Riemann map explicitly. Such maps therefore satisfy an algebraic ODE through their Schwarzian derivative.
For circular-arc polygons, the map from the disk is a ratio of solutions of a second-order linear ODE. This is again a special boundary class where differential algebraicity holds.

Related theme: S. Bell characterizes 'algebraic domains' (which admit an algebraic proper map onto the disc) through algebraic Bergman or Szegő kernels. This is a different algebraicity notion from Hilbert's.

triage.why: The note poses a clear research question: are Riemann maps of domains bounded by algebraic ovals differentially algebraic? The idea is close to Hilbert's interests in differential transcendence (Hölder's Gamma theorem, and his 1900 problems 18/22 on uniformization). However, it is not one of the 23 problems, and it is not the 24th either. The sources I found cover only special boundary classes where an ODE exists (polygons, circular-arc polygons) and nearby questions (o-minimality, algebraic kernels). None of them settle the general claim in either direction. Search capacity ran out before I could look specifically for later work by Lindemann, Schwarz or others, or for modern hypertranscendence results on Riemann maps, so I cannot say whether it was answered later. The verdict 'possibly_unexplored' reflects missing evidence, not a confirmed absence of literature.
